No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. She spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. With a swift motion, she scoops up Finley in her net and pulls him out of the water.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley thrashes about in the net, his scales glinting in the sunlight.

CUT TO:

INT. JEN'S CAR - DAY

Jen carefully places Finley in a specialized container filled with water, which she then places on the passenger seat. She adjusts her rearview mirror to get a better look at Finley.

JEN
(to herself)
I'm going to show you something amazing.

As they drive to a remote location, the sky begins to darken. Finley, sensing the change, becomes agitated, swimming frantically in his container.

CUT TO:

EXT. REMOTE LOCATION - DAY

Jen parks the car and steps out, Finley's container in hand. She sets it down on a nearby rock, and Finley is forced to stare up at the sky.

The sun begins to dip below the horizon, casting a shadow on the ground. Finley's eyes widen in terror as the moon begins to cover the sun, creating an otherworldly glow.

FINLEY (V.O.)
(whispering)
What...what is this? A...a...a... (gulps) a...a...a...thing?

Jen stands beside him, a mixture of fascination and concern on her face.

JEN
(whispering)
It's a solar eclipse, Finley. It's a rare phenomenon.

FINLEY (V.O.)
( growing more agitated)
Phenomenon?! You call this a phenomenon?! This is...this is... (gulps) this is... (stammers) this is...HORRORS BEYOND MY COMPREHENSION!

Finley's voice rises to a frantic pitch as he begins to thrash about in his container.

CUT TO:

INT. JEN'S CAR - DAY

Finley's monologue becomes a cacophony of terror and despair.

FINLEY (V.O.)
(whispering)
I am but a mere fish, a insignificant speck in the grand tapestry of existence. And yet, I am forced to confront...to confront... (gulps) the abyssal void that lies beyond the veil of reality!

Jen's expression changes from fascination to concern as Finley's words become more and more unhinged.

JEN
(alarmed)
Finley, calm down! It's okay!

FINLEY (V.O.)
(whispering)
No, it's not okay! It's not okay at all! (gulps) I am but a fleeting moment in the grand dance of time, a moment that will soon be extinguished like a candle in the wind!

Finley's container begins to rattle and shake as he becomes more and more agitated.

CUT TO:

EXT. REMOTE LOCATION - DAY

Jen tries to calm Finley down, but he's beyond consolation.

FINLEY (V.O.)
(whispering)
I am but a mere mortal, a fragile shell of consciousness in an uncaring universe. And yet, I am forced to confront...to confront... (gulps) the eldritch horrors that lurk beyond the veil of sanity!

As the eclipse reaches its peak, Finley's monologue becomes a chilling, Lovecraftian incantation.

FINLEY (V.O.)
(whispering)
Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Cthulhu R'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn! (In his house at R'lyeh, dead Cthulhu waits dreaming!)

The camera zooms in on Finley's terrified face as the eclipse reaches its climax.

CUT TO:

EXT. REMOTE LOCATION - DAY

As the eclipse ends, Finley's container lies still, his eyes frozen in terror. Jen looks on, concerned.

JEN
(whispering)
Finley, are you okay?

Finley's response is a mere whisper, a faint echo of his former self.

FINLEY (V.O.)
(whispering)
I...I...I am no more. I am but a shell, a husk of a being, forever changed by the horrors I have beheld.

The camera lingers on Finley's container, the only sound the gentle lapping of the waves against the shore.

FADE TO BLACK.
